subject: Materials Science
title: Silicon Carbide: Hard as Diamond
description: A short lesson to help you apply Silicon Carbide: Hard as Diamond.

hook.text: Sandpaper that grinds steel uses grains of silicon carbide — nearly as hard as diamond.

buildup.text: SiC is a covalent ceramic — silicon and carbon bonded in a tetrahedral lattice.

discovery.text: It stays hard at 1,600°C, making it perfect for furnace linings and brake rotors.

twist.text: SiC is also a semiconductor — power electronics use it to handle voltages silicon can't.

climax.text: Electric vehicle inverters increasingly use SiC chips for higher efficiency and range.

punchline.text: One ceramic grinds metal and runs power electronics.

quiz.question: Why is silicon carbide used in EV power electronics?
options: It handles higher voltages and temperatures than silicon
It is softer and easier to fabricate
